Runtime and execution events

Read telemetry, executor outcomes, subagent startup checks, relay state and service recovery events.

About 33 min read · 6 sections

On this page

Return to the diagnostics overview.

Local telemetry

provider_connection_recovered records a Chat Completions connection that obtained an HTTP response after transient retries: provider, attempts, elapsedMs and httpStatus only. It proves restored transport reachability; request_completed remains the evidence that inference actually finished. Tailnet connection failures retain allowlisted network codes and the fixed connect stage, so temporary DNS and dial timeouts can be distinguished from certificate failures without recording addresses or exception prose.

chat_overflow_guard reports outcome: refused with the provider ID when a Chat Completions conversation hit 25 consecutive context overflows within ten minutes and Gateway refused its next request locally with a non-retryable invalid_request. The count lives in memory per provider and conversation, resets on any completed request, and expires after ten quiet minutes. See cache safety.

context_cache_guard reports outcome: blocked (or observed for a selfHosted provider, which continues), mode: seed|oneshot|continued|provider, a hashed threadKey and a numeric rewrites count. It appears in recent problems when the shared guard stops another large uncached request before inference. See cache safety.

Each process appends one JSON line per event to <state>/telemetry/events-YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl (mode 0600, kept 14 days). Fields pass a strict filter: only strings, numbers and booleans; names that could carry secrets or content (token, prompt, body, content, text, input, argument, env, header, auth) are dropped, except numeric token counts; text is reduced to a safe character set and home paths to their last segment. Error text is never stored, only a fixed class such as stream_disconnected, usage_limit, rate_limit or attachment (a queued or attached local file the engine could not read). A status code such as 503 counts as overloaded only as a standalone number, never as digits inside a chat id.

Process Events
Adapter turn_started, turn_completed, turn_empty_completion (completed with no answer and no tool call), turn_error, turn_quiet (no events for five minutes), rpc_error, adapter_client (client and clientVersion, the names the desktop gave in initialize), adapter_session_end (durationMs, requests and nativeClosed, whether the native engine had already closed), adapter_start_failed (errorClass and code, such as -32001 when a required host is unavailable: the adapter could not start its engines; a host that is restarting, busy or owned elsewhere is not also reported as an exception), native_catalog_incomplete (exactly missing, a count, and optionally cacheVersionMatches; recorded once per adapter start when the native model cache lacks models the engine lists), native_relay_skipped (exactly reason: not_registered, not_connected or unreachable; the adapter or SSH listener starts without routing to the native relay; with not_registered the engine keeps its own remote control, and from 0.4.8 with not_connected or unreachable it does not, because a registered relay owns remote control; once per process, see when the relay is set aside), native_activation_refused (exactly reason, recorded by gateway native install under a unified plan before anything changed or after a clean rollback: app_running (ChatGPT was open), listener_busy (an SSH listener had a request or turn in flight, or declined to retire), listener_unknown (a listener kept no usable activity record, such as one from a release before 0.4.8, or its start time no longer matches), adapter_running (another Codex session on this Mac holds an engine), listener_stuck (a listener that agreed to retire did not exit in 10 s), host_busy (the shared host's native engine did not stand down within 30 s), process_list (the process list could not be read or parsed) or signal_failed (asking a listener to retire failed)), native_activation_failed (exactly reason: timeout, exit, start or other; the relay's --enable did not connect, and the previous registration was kept byte for byte), native_listener_retired (exactly count: idle SSH listeners that retired themselves before --enable), ssh_listener_retire_request (exactly outcome, retired or declined: recorded by an SSH listener when an activation asked it to retire; it retires only if no request is in flight, no turn runs and it has been silent for 30 s), engine_exit (engine, code, signal, uptimeMs, activeTurns, initiatedBy and reason: one engine process this adapter spawned ended, once per process), engine_frame_dropped (engine and sizeMiB), engine_frame_invalid (engine), engine_message_failed (engine, and method only when it is a plain method name), native_turns_evicted (count; at most once a minute), execution_host_control_lost (exactly sharedGateway: the executor host closed this desktop session's control connection, so the session ended and the app reconnects and acquires a fresh one, see the shared host's control connection); the engine events are explained in engine exits, native_sharing_fallback (exactly reason and holders: reason is host_unavailable when the plan shares native chats but the host stayed down through the adapter's wait and no live native owner remained, so this adapter took a private native-home lease and started its own native engine, other when the host runs without native sharing, so this adapter started its own native engine and kept gateway chats on the host, or native_owner when a running host with native sharing refused native ownership because private engines that ran while it was down still hold the native home, so this adapter joined them with its own engine instead of failing; holders is a number only, how many private engines held the native home once this adapter's lease was taken, this one included: private engines share the home with each other and never with the host's native writer, see native fallback; recorded only once the fallback was allowed), compaction_switch_refused (exactly sourceFamily, targetFamily, measuredTokens, estimatedTokens and limitTokens: a turn that switched a gateway chat to another tokenizer was refused before it was sent, because the last measurement recounted for the selected model would not fit its usable window; see compaction), model_switch_promoted (no fields: with midTurnModelSwitch on, a picker model change was also applied to the running gateway turn), model_switch_deferred (exactly reason: context when the tokenizer recount refused it, review_group when the SDK's active-step check refused it, not_applied or error; the change still applies from the next turn; see mid-turn model changes), reasoning_restored (provider gateway, method and source record, rollout or thread of a gateway chat's recovered effort, adjusted; native chats are never restored by the adapter, so 0.4.1 no longer logs provider: native), reasoning_effort_reset (from, to, model and method when a restored level had to be fitted), reasoning_unrecovered (model when no effort could be recovered), gateway_features_trimmed (exactly site, one of request, spawn, home or retry, and count: how many feature settings were dropped, reduced to a boolean or rewritten so the pinned gateway SDK accepts them; a structured table that had fields removed also counts, once per entry however many fields went; retry is the strict form sent once after the SDK refused a thread request's configuration; never names or values; only when count is above zero), service_tier_dropped (exactly model, tier and method: a speed tier the selected gateway row does not offer was dropped, so the session starts as Standard; method is thread/start, thread/resume or thread/fork; tier is one of priority, fast or a tier id from the gateway model catalog, and any other value is logged as other; Flex is never dropped, so it is never logged; recorded only after the SDK accepted the request, and only when the SDK's answer carries no tier, null or default, because a loaded chat that kept its tier was not dropped), ssh_listener_upgrade_requested (exactly from and to releases: an SSH proxy found the listener behind its connection on another release than the installed one and asked it to retire when idle; once per proxy; from is unknown for a lease without a release; the listener itself records ssh_listener_retire_request with the outcome), ssh_listener_replaced (from and to releases, no paths: a bootstrap on the installed release replaced a remote listener that was running another release; from is unknown when that listener recorded no release, which means it started from a checkout or from a release before 0.4.4, so the first 0.4.4 rollout logs from: "unknown" for every listener it replaces), gateway_chat_classified (exactly rule and method: rule is the first rule that identified the chat, legacy_provider, registry, parent, alias or native, in the order the adapter checks them, and native when none matched; method is the request or notification that made the adapter classify the chat, one of thread/start, thread/resume, thread/fork, thread/read, turn/start, turn/steer, turn/interrupt, thread/settings/update, turn/settings/update, thread/settings/updated, thread/unsubscribe or compaction, and any other method is logged as other; recorded once per chat per desktop connection, never with a chat id), gateway_registry_write_failed (no fields: the adapter could not write a gateway chat to its registry; recorded once per connection; a chat saved as subscription_gateway is still identified by that id, and one saved as openai through its gateway alias or, for a sub-agent, the ancestor chats the adapter reads, see harness identity), gateway_alias_unscoped (exactly count: how many configured model aliases have no /, such as claude/sonnet, so a native model added later with the same name would take their place; recorded once per process), gateway_registry_unreadable (no fields: the registry file could not be read, so it counted as empty; recorded once per registry, and the next write sets the unreadable file aside as <scope>.json.unreadable), executor_reattached (exactly reason, ms and requests: a gateway chat whose executor was gone was loaded again on a live one before its request was sent, see re-attaching a gateway chat; reason is engine_closed when the host went away or a private executor exited, or generation_retired when the host was still connected but no longer served this connection; ms is how long the re-attach took and requests how many requests waited for it; never a chat id, model or path), executor_reattach_failed (exactly reason and requests: the re-attach failed and the request got the old -32001 error; reason is host_unavailable when the shared host could not be found or asked within the wait, or resume_failed when the gateway refused to provide an executor for the chat (for example its catalog, generation limit or a changed provider) or the executor refused to resume it; while a host_unavailable fail-fast window is open, refused requests raise the same error but record nothing, so one window logs the reason at most once, and a host lookup that finds the host alive ends the window). The turn records (turn_started, turn_completed, turn_empty_completion, turn_error and turn_quiet) of a gateway chat also carry identity: legacy when the chat was saved with the gateway's own provider id (gatefox, or subscription_gateway before 1.8.0), and openai when it was saved with the native identity; native chats carry no identity
Chat Completions chat_request_rejected (provider, a fixed reason and an allowlisted param for every HTTP 400 from a Chat Completions server; never its message)
Adapter startup codex_home_ignored (reason: gateway_internal: an inherited gateway-internal CODEX_HOME was dropped so the adapter reads the native home)
Server request_completed, request_empty, request_failed (queue time, time to first event, tool calls, input, cached, cache-write, reasoning and output tokens, providerType, Copilot nanoAiu credits with nanoAiuStatus and the initiator of its model calls (user, agent or mixed), whether a Codex turn-state was echoed and returned, and abortCause such as shutdown; when one connection attempt held more than one transient code, networkCodes names them in sorted, comma-joined form; a context_length_exceeded whose provider reported its native counts adds contextUsedTokens and contextMaximumTokens), request_unsupported (a Messages count_tokens call, which the gateway declines with a 501: requestId, route and endpoint only, with no request_failed and no stderr line), provider_retry (the real attempt about to run, its code, elapsedMs since the first failure, backoffMs, the upstreamCode or — when happy-eyeballs tried both address families and their codes differed — the sorted comma-joined networkCodes, and upstreamStage), provider_recovered (provider, attempts and elapsedMs: a request that finished after at least one transient connection retry), tool_search_dropped (exactly provider, tools and items: a tool_search tool or replayed tool_search_call / tool_search_output items were removed, by the Codex subscription route without the bridge before sending upstream, because the ChatGPT backend refuses a forwarded tool_search, or by any other route before translation, so a chat that switched from a Codex route keeps working; counts only, never a definition, query or argument; only when something was dropped, see tool search), tool_search_bridged (exactly provider, tools, calls, outputs and loaded: a Codex subscription route with "toolSearch": "bridge" sent the client's search declarations, replayed calls and outputs as function items, and declared loaded tools that earlier searches returned; counts only, never a name, query or definition; once per request and only when the request carried search), web_search_dropped (exactly provider, tools and items: a route that does not forward the hosted web_search tool removed a web_search tool or replayed web_search_call items before translation, so a chat that switched from the Codex subscription route keeps working; counts only, never a name, query or result; only when something was dropped, see hosted web search), tool_declarations_merged (exactly replaced and identical: a request declared the same tool more than once, in additional_tools input items or again in its top-level tools, and the gateway merged them into its catalog instead of refusing the request; counts only, never a tool name or definition; once per request and only when something merged, see repeated tool declarations), claude_cli (mode, toolCalls, input, cache read and write, and output tokens, interrupted, retry, threadKey — the same first 8 hex claude_session reports, when the request carried a thread id, so one thread's one-shot and live events line up — and systemPrefixOnly set when its cache read reached only the system prefix, the same test claude_session applies below; also on tool turns and cancellations), claude_session (live sessions: outcome such as spawned, continued, reseeded, preserved, fallback, interrupted, reaped, evicted or crashed, the miss reason (a fallback outcome carries warmup before a thread has completed its configured admission requests, capacity when every slot held a warm session, or session_dead for a crashed-session replay hold; preserved reports prefix_diverged, unexpected_tail, forced_choice or effort_midturn when a request is refused without closing the session or starting inference), cache read and write, input and output tokens, threadKey — the first 8 hex of the thread's session key — afterWarmup on a spawned session promoted after its warmup, changed on a fingerprint_changed reseed (a comma-separated subset of model, thinking, fast, instructions and tools; contract when only a release changed the fingerprint's meaning; unknown for a session started before 1.6.0) with toolsAdded, toolsRemoved and toolsEdited counts when the tools changed, never a tool name, and systemPrefixOnly on a spawn or reseed that read only the system prefix — reported once the request's cache read plus write pass that prefix by a margin, since the threshold (32,035 tokens) is calibrated to the Codex system prefix and a shorter prompt says nothing either way), copilot_session (live Copilot sessions, on by default: outcome spawned, continued, reseeded, fallback, interrupted, reaped, evicted, crashed or closed; missReason, which is the reseed or fallback reason of a request and the reason a session ended; threadKey; liveSessions; divergedAt; parkedMs; failed; and the request's own initiator (user, agent or mixed), inputTokens, cacheReadTokens, cacheWriteTokens, outputTokens, reasoningTokens, nanoAiu and toolCalls; every outcome, field and reason is listed in live Copilot sessions), model_alias_resolved, server_hot_swap, config_rejected (exactly reason: why a change to gateway.json was not applied, so the last good configuration keeps serving every model: rebind when an existing model alias would change its provider, account, credential source, base URL or upstream model, restart_required when the port, mode or state directory changed, invalid when the file does not parse or validate, or unreadable when it cannot be read; once per file version, never with a path, value or error text, and listed among the recent problems of gateway diagnostics; /health reports the same word as configRejected while the change stays refused, and a valid refused file still stops the aliases it removed; a later valid, allowed file is applied and clears it, and the first load at startup still fails, see architecture), provider_address_refused (exactly provider and reason not_tailnet: a provider with "tailnet": true resolved its host to an address outside Tailscale (100.64.0.0/10, fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48), on inference or model discovery; that address was dropped before any connection, so the key was not sent to it; never the address or host; if no Tailscale address remained the call failed with provider_unreachable 502, while a Tailscale router that does not answer is the retryable upstream_unavailable 503), model_metadata_refreshed, model_metadata_skipped (the six-hour metadata refresh left one provider out: provider and a fixed reason, refresh_deferred when serving a Codex login's access token would need a refresh (it has expired, or expires within two minutes unless the issuer's earliest_refresh_at is still in the future) and the refresh was left to the next real request, or discovery_failed for any other failure; the error text is never recorded), server_shutdown_signal, server_drain (requests drained, drain time, requests aborted)
Server, Claude Desktop claude_direct_route (alias and variant: a Messages request named a Claude-safe route ID that the gateway resolved to that alias; variant is true for a hidden effort or speed alias; see direct serving)
Server request fields Every request_completed, request_empty and request_failed record uses model for the resolved catalog alias. It includes requestedModel only when the caller used a different name, and clientProtocol is either responses or messages.
Service component_exit (component, kind, code, uptimeMs and restarts; a desktop setup that exits 0 is not an exit), component_paused (the optional native relay was set aside: component, kind and a fixed reason — not_registered when <state>/native-registration.json is missing or says the relay is gone, failing after three non-zero exits in a row, each within 60 s of its start, or after one such exit following a resume that has not yet run past its first minute; a signal death or a binary that never spawned counts as one; once a slot is paused nothing more is logged until the next re-check starts it), component_resumed (component and kind: a paused relay was started again by the five minute re-check, which also restarts a relay that is still failing every half hour), component_failing (an inference or tunnel child exited within 60 s of its start five times in a row: component, kind, failures (5) and reason, exit_<code>, signal_<NAME> or spawn_failed; once per streak, and a run of a minute or more ends the streak; the component stays waiting between starts and keeps its backoff), execution_host_failed (failures and reason, see service self-heal), execution_host_recovered (failures before the start that worked), execution_host_unhealthy (reason of the second of two failed probes in a row of the running host, once until the reason changes or a probe passes), execution_host_restarted (reason: the probe's, or relay_registered when a host that started before the relay was registered restarts while idle so its native engine stands down; only the host was stopped, while idle, and started again; 0.4.7 and earlier also logged relay_paused), execution_owner_reclaimed (scope: host, native_home or generation; reason: previous_boot, dead_pids or invalid_receipt; a dead owner's receipt was moved aside, see architecture), status_write_failed (exactly code, an errno name such as ENOSPC or EACCES, or other; at most once a minute), login_consolidation_completed (jobs: an interrupted next-login consolidation passed its checks and was finished and promoted at the daemon's start), login_consolidation_restored (jobs: how many original login jobs were put back after an interrupted next-login consolidation failed its checks; started and failed: how many of the restored jobs other than the primary one were loaded at once, or failed to load), native_acquire (outcome: attached, launched, replaced, refused, refused_busy, or refused_owner when another live owner, such as a desktop's private native engine, still holds the native home; relation of the requested launch to the running one, same, subset, superset or conflict, on every outcome but launched and refused_owner; busyChats on replaced and refused_busy; richerLaunchReused on launched), native_sharing_unavailable (exactly reason: sdk_version, sdk_signature or other; the host started without native sharing because the app's native engine was not the verified one; native_owner: the native home had another live or unconfirmed owner when the host started, so the host serves gateway chats and claims the native home at the next native request instead; native_identity: a dead owner's native-home receipt names another configuration or another spelling of the native home, so the host serves gateway chats and refuses each native request with Native execution ownership changed until that receipt is moved aside), system_wake (sleptSeconds), executor_turn_settled (shared-engine outcomes; see executor outcomes), desktop_api_mode (action: on, off or preset; outcome: applied, refused, rolled_back, failed or skipped; reason is one fixed code and never a path, model, configuration value or environment value: app_running, already_on, not_on, client_only, foreign_cli_path, native_write, clear_cli_path or rollback. on/off records what that call did; preset/skipped is logged once per process when an adapter path stood down because API mode owns the desktop, see API mode), tunnel_stale_listener_cleared (component and processes), sharing_disabled (mode), sharing_disable_failed (mode and outcome, how the failed change was undone), release_skew_refused (exactly direction and count: the host refused a generation request whose gateway SDK is not its own, because the app and the service run different releases; direction is adapter_newer when the adapter's SDK is the installed, newer release's (read from that release's gateway-sdk/build.json): the service has not moved yet, the adapter is told "This Mac's gateway service is moving to the newer release; this chat continues as soon as no turn is running", and that release's move becomes urgent; it is adapter_older otherwise, or when the direction could not be told: the service already moved, and the adapter is told "This app and this Mac's gateway service run different gateway releases; quit and reopen ChatGPT to load the installed release"; count is the refusals since the last record; at most once per direction; see services), execution_host_quiet_upgrade (exactly loadedChats, a count: after a live controller update the execution host moved to the new implementation when its chats drained, without the strict idle gate; see services), execution_host_upgrade_waiting (exactly reason, the quiet check's fixed vocabulary as in self_upgrade_waiting; once per reason per pending move), execution_generation_forward (exactly to, a release: an older service spawned a generation on the installed release's gateway SDK, verified by that release's own verifier, for a newer adapter instead of refusing it; see services), execution_request_failed (exactly method, the control method such as execution/acquire, or other, and reason, the same fixed class as execution_host_failed: the host refused a control request with an error whose own text it does not pass through, so the adapter was told "Execution operation failed (reason); managed chat ownership was preserved"; never the error's text, a path or a value; see services), self_upgrade (from and to releases; the moved process names itself in component: adapter, service, server, or ssh_listener when an idle SSH listener retired itself after an install; a listener replaced by a bootstrap logs ssh_listener_replaced on the Adapter row instead; mode: idle for a move at an idle moment, which is every move but the service's quiet and skew ones, quiet when the service moved under the quiet rule after the release had waited 15 minutes, or skew when it moved urgently because the host had refused an adapter of the installed release, with no 15 minute grace and no wait for recently ended turns (only a running turn, a pending approval or input, a background terminal or busy inference held it back), see services; loadedChats on quiet and skew: how many chats the host's engines still had loaded, a count), self_upgrade_waiting (from and to releases and exactly reason, why a quiet upgrade attempt after the 15 minute grace, or at once for an urgent move, did not restart the service: running (a turn is running or waiting for an approval or input), background_terminal (a chat keeps a background terminal, such as a dev server an agent left running), recent_turn (a turn ended within the last 5 minutes), ephemeral_settling (a throwaway chat, or one that has saved nothing yet, has not been seen settled for 5 minutes), unreadable (an engine, a chat or its status could not be read), too_many (more than 256 loaded chats in one engine) or inference_busy (the host was quiet but inference refused its idle guard), or handover_busy (a live controller swap was refused for a host probe, start or restart check through all its quick retries, since 1.5.8); each reason once per pending release, see services)

The Adapter row records unix_session_end for each accepted Unix connection: process-local sessionId, fixed cause, numeric closeCode, and durationMs. gateway diagnostics groups these under connectionEnds by cause and close code. Local session completion/failure and listener shutdown are distinct from an unclassified transport close; code 1006 alone does not identify a network fault. Peer close-reason strings and exception text are never recorded. See remote connection diagnosis.

The Adapter row also records completion_replayed with exactly outcome: delivered, stale, turn_changed, not_terminal, already_delivered_in_session, or lookup_failed.

Claude consolidation records only its fixed lifecycle events: claude_consolidation_staged, claude_consolidation_activated, claude_consolidation_deferred, claude_consolidation_rolled_back and claude_consolidation_failed. Their fields are numeric job counts or fixed reason/phase names, never plist contents, command arguments or environment values. self_upgrade_waiting can also report claude_busy when a Claude child's connection check refuses a service restart or cannot be answered.

A chat that an engine starts on its own, such as a sub-agent or a review, has no route on this connection. Its turn records take provider from the engine that announced the chat, model from its thread/started notification (updated by later thread/settings/updated notifications), and identity by the same rule as routed gateway chats. Earlier releases logged these turns as provider: "unknown" with no model. A chat that has a route always reports its route.

An adapter rpc_error records the method, the JSON-RPC code and either reason (the adapter's own fixed routing message) or errorClass. It also records rejection, named from the engine's or adapter's message, which is itself never stored: adapter_routing, unknown_method, experimental_api, invalid_params, relative_path (a path such as the desktop's projectless ~ that is not absolute), prediction_fork_overrides, prediction_fork_parent, no_active_process, process_not_running, duplicate_process_handle, spawn_failed, rollout_not_found, thread_not_loaded, thread_not_persisted, engine_closed, engine_timeout, or other. gateway diagnostics groups non-routing RPC errors by rejection when it is more specific than other (and by errorClass otherwise); adapter routing errors stay grouped by their fixed reason.

Verified native file-read failures distinguish file_not_found from path_permission_denied. Native process startup distinguishes spawn_path_missing from spawn_permission_denied; a missing program and a missing working directory share the same native error, so the gateway does not guess which one was absent. Classification is restricted to exact known method, code and message combinations. Replies and caller paths remain unchanged, every failure remains in diagnostics, and permission failures are not treated as benign misses. These names do not alter the watchdog's separate session-refusal rules.

A request whose Codex login refresh was answered with an HTTP error status (400, 401 or 403 for a rejected login; any other HTTP error status, for example 429 or 5xx, for a temporary failure) records request_failed with upstreamEvent oauth_refresh and upstreamCode set to the OAuth error code the token endpoint returned: one of invalid_grant, refresh_token_reused, refresh_token_expired, refresh_token_invalidated, invalid_request, invalid_client, unauthorized_client, unsupported_grant_type, invalid_scope, access_denied, invalid_token, token_expired, server_error, temporarily_unavailable, slow_down, rate_limit_exceeded, other for any code outside that list, or none when the reply carried no code. Only the code is kept; the reply's description, body and tokens are never recorded or shown. Other refresh failures record only code and status. A temporary upstream_unavailable 503 covers a network error, a busy refresh lock, an unreadable or malformed reply, and a credential file that could not be written after a successful reply. authentication 401 means the stored login needs the user to sign in: there is no login, the credential file is unreadable, the stored login has no refresh token or lacks the plan scopes, or a refresh reply lacked the plan scopes. A failed refresh is never retried inside the request, so the single-use refresh token is spent once and no provider_retry follows it.

A Responses request that succeeds after retries records provider_recovered with provider, class (network or throttle), attempts and elapsedMs from the first failure of that class. Throttle provider_retry events carry code: "rate_limit_exceeded", the wait in backoffMs, and the time since the first throttle in elapsedMs.

A request the gateway could not translate records the same request_failed event plus two fixed fields: reason is one of invalid_shape, unsupported_input_item, unsupported_content, unsupported_role, invalid_tool_call, unsupported_tool, duplicate_tool, unsupported_tool_choice, invalid_image, invalid_reasoning_state, invalid_instructions, invalid_provider_output; itemType names the rejected item or tool type, but only from a fixed allowlist of Responses wire types, and as other for anything the list does not contain. A value outside those sets is dropped rather than recorded, so no caller text, tool name, or identifier can ride in on them. gateway diagnostics groups those failures by code and reason, which separates a malformed request from an unsupported item without storing either's contents. The message the client receives stays "Responses request contains invalid or unsupported data" whatever the reason.

gateway diagnostics [--since HOURS] summarizes the log: turn outcomes and failure classes per model, request outcomes, cache-hit ratio and first-event latency per model, turn outcomes the shared executor recorded itself (executorTurns, per engine, status and error class), Auto-review requests (autoReview, below), retries (keyed by the socket code they reported, or by the sorted networkCodes set when one connection attempt held more than one), RPC errors, component exits, host events (every execution_host_* event and native_acquire outcome), live Claude sessions per outcome (and per miss reason) with their cache reads, writes and a rewrite count — the spawns and reseeds whose cache read reached only the system prefix — and the 25 most recent problems: failed, empty and quiet turns, executor turns that failed or carried an error, failed (not cancelled) and empty requests, RPC errors, component exits, adapter_start_failed, execution_host_failed, and the self-heal reports component_failing, execution_host_unhealthy and status_write_failed. Set GATEWAY_TELEMETRY=off to disable the log.

Executor outcomes without a window

executor_turn_settled records a terminal turn from a shared gateway or native engine. Its fields are engine, threadId, turnId, the SDK's status, a fixed errorClass when the turn carries an error, and durationMs when both timestamps are available. Error text and chat contents are never logged. An SDK status of completed with an attached error remains distinguishable by its error class.

The service inspects engines every 30 seconds through short-lived connections, as its existing activity checks do. It validates socket ownership, ignores server callbacks, and closes each inspection client. Inspection never creates or resumes a chat or executes a tool. Bounded batches and pagination limit work; failed reads remain pending for a later inspection. Recent terminal turns can be collected even when another turn is already running. Old idle histories are skipped when their timestamps conclusively predate this host's tracking window. Each pass handles up to 32 chats and 16 history pages, with a 96-request ceiling and a ten-second deadline. Busy batches rotate fairly; a new head arriving during a history walk remains pending for a fresh head scan.

gateway diagnostics reports these observations separately as executorTurns and includes failed or error-carrying outcomes in recentProblems. It does not add them to the adapter's turns counts, because an attached adapter may have observed the same turn. This is best-effort diagnostics, not a complete audit: throwaway histories, unavailable metadata, work outside the tracking window, and chats never observed by the inspector can remain unavailable.

Verify automatic collection against an isolated real SDK with:

node scripts/e2e-chat-state.mjs --package /absolute/verified/package \
  --root /tmp/task-specific-evidence --executor-diagnostics

The fixture uses a local mock provider. It disconnects both application clients before a synthetic subscription-limit failure, waits for the host's inspection, then compares the recorded error class and outcome with the persisted SDK turn. It uses no account or paid inference and does not modify production chats.

A request whose model is the reviewer codex-auto-review carries autoReview: true on request_completed, request_empty and request_failed, including its 404. Gateway executors send every Auto-review approval there (node_repl, shell, apply_patch, network, MCP and permissions), so gateway diagnostics counts them together in an autoReview bucket: completed, empty and failed:<code> (node_repl).

Subagent startup checks

An agent's pending_init status alone does not establish a model startup failure. On 23 October 2026, a Qwen child reported that status even though its saved turn contained model output and 16 executed tool calls. Another child had no model output and no terminal error, so those records do not establish its failure cause. A fresh Qwen role check subsequently executed a command and returned its result. Check actual turn events and tool results before attributing a failure to login, model routing, or the provider. Delays and missing terminal events need separate investigation; do not turn a status observation into a claimed authentication error.

scripts/e2e-subagent-sidebar.mjs --v2 --openai verifies real SDK delegation, child tool execution, readable history, queued messages, and follow-up work with mock inference. Add --accounts to require every bare-model child request to use the designated account while two Codex accounts offer the same model. This does not test real provider latency or the desktop's rendering.

Add --role-fork with --v2 to verify a named role selects its configured model during a full-history fork, without an explicit spawn-model override. The fixture keeps the default child model equal to the parent, requires a parent-only history marker in child inference, and checks real child tool work, saved model, reasoning and follow-up. It uses the installed SDK with local mock inference. Legacy MultiAgentV1 rejects named-role overrides on full-history forks. The 26 October 2026 receipt records the installed SDK check and matching actual binary hashes on all three Macs.

When the relay is set aside

The native relay is optional, so a machine without a working one is not broken. A service slot that owns the relay reports component_paused once and then says nothing at all: no exit, no restart and no log line, until something changes. gateway service status shows the slot as paused with its reason, and a paused slot has no process to print, so gateway versions simply leaves it out. A relay whose log cannot be opened is set aside at once, without waiting for three exits. The service looks again every five minutes and starts the relay once a registration exists, no ChatGPT app is open, and the binaries or the registration changed since the pause — or, with nothing changed at all, once half an hour has passed since it was set aside, so a brief start-up problem never pauses a working relay for good. That start reports component_resumed. A resumed relay is out of retries: one more non-zero exit within a minute of its start sets it aside again at once, so a relay that cannot run costs at most two starts an hour. A resumed relay that runs past its first minute has proved itself and gets three strikes again. A re-check whose questions cannot all be answered leaves the rest of the service untouched: a process list that will not come counts as an open app, so the slot simply stays paused with no new event, and only a probe that throws sets the slot paused again as failing (one component_paused). When the shared execution host started while the relay still looked usable, it took the machine's remote-control registration for the relay. From 0.4.8 a registered relay owns remote control even while it is set aside: the host and every adapter keep their engines' remote control off whenever the relay is registered or an activation is pending, so no other engine takes the one remote-control connection the Mac has (another holder made the relay's connect fail with 409 Conflict). The phone cannot reach that Mac until the relay is back; gateway health warns once the relay has been registered but paused or not connected for five minutes, and gateway native uninstall gives remote control back to ChatGPT. (0.4.7 and earlier restarted the host with reason relay_paused to hand remote control back instead.) An adapter decides once when it starts and records native_relay_skipped when the relay it was registered for is not connected or not reachable, so a relay that comes up later is used from the next app start or the next listener start. Consolidation and the shared-service migrations accept a paused relay as ready, and wait for a relay to connect only where a registration says one is set up and its relay slot is actually running. See the app-server adapter.

Service self-heal

The unified service repairs its own parts without restarting the others. Each event below carries fixed words and counts only, never paths, error text or environment values.

Event When What the service does
status_write_failed service-status.json could not be written (a full disk, a read-only folder). Keeps running; the status file is advisory. The next five-second heartbeat writes again. Reported at most once a minute.
execution_host_failed A shared execution host start failed. Retries after 1, 2, 5, 10 and 30 s, then every 60 s. Inference, tunnels and the relay keep running.
execution_host_unhealthy The running host failed two probes in a row; the probe runs every 60 s and on an adapter's kick. Restarts only the host, and only while it is idle; a busy host is probed again a minute later. A probe that passes again cancels the restart.
execution_host_restarted An idle host was stopped and started again. A start that then fails reports execution_host_failed and backs off as above.
component_failing An inference or tunnel child exited within 60 s of its start five times in a row. Keeps restarting it with its usual backoff (up to 30 s), so a passing fault heals; the event is not repeated during the streak.
desktop_env_agent_failed The unified service's desktop setup (desktop-restore, or a registration while a unified or staged plan owns it) could not remove the 0.4.7 login environment agent it no longer keeps, or found a plist at its label that is not the gateway's. reason is unmanaged (that plist is left alone) or other (the removal failed). Keeps going: CODEX_CLI_PATH is already set, no agent is needed beside the unified service, and the registration reports envAgent: false and loginEnv: "service". The next service start tries again. On a Mac with a unified or staged plan, gateway desktop register run by hand takes the same path (event recorded under component service). Only without a plan does a hand-run register write the agent, fail loudly and report no event.
desktop_env_preset_failed The service daemon's first step could not set CODEX_CLI_PATH for the login session. reason is read (the receipt or the session's current value could not be read) or setenv (the launchctl setenv failed). A foreign value, a missing wrapper or a missing release runtime are not failures and record nothing. Keeps going: the daemon starts normally and the desktop-restore child sets the variable a little later, so only an app that launched in between runs without the gateway until it is restarted. No value or path is recorded.
login_consolidation_completed A --next-login consolidation was interrupted after its last file write (its staging process is gone) and passed the promotion checks at the daemon's start. Promotes the plan and runs it.
login_consolidation_restored Such a consolidation failed a promotion check instead (jobs put back; started and failed, the restored jobs other than the primary one that were loaded at once or failed to load). A check that only means "not yet" (an old job still loaded, or a start that is not launchd's primary job) records nothing and leaves the staging for the next start. Puts the original login jobs back, loads all but the primary one at once, and stays idle, across relaunches, until the next login; each relaunch loads, again, a restored job that is still not loaded. See services for the recovery.

execution_host_failed names its reason from a fixed set, never the error text:

Reason Meaning Retried by a kick
live_owner Another live host or writer still owns the folder, a generation or the native home. Once per backoff step
identity_changed The folder's live owner has another configuration, native home, engine or socket. Once per backoff step
receipt_invalid An ownership receipt is invalid and its owner cannot be proven gone. Once per backoff step
sdk_invalid The engine binary is missing, changed, unsigned or the wrong version. Once per backoff step
sdk_dir_missing The SDK socket folder (/tmp/codex-daemon-<uid>) is gone, as after a reboot. Each kick, five seconds apart
socket_occupied A socket path is held by another listener. Each kick, five seconds apart
io_error A file system error, such as a folder with the wrong permissions. Each kick, five seconds apart
other Anything else. Each kick, five seconds apart
close_failed An idle host restart could not close the old host, whose receipt still names the running service. Never: no host starts in that process again. The service restarts as a whole once inference is idle, asked again every 60 s.

An adapter that finds the host down writes the private kick file in the host folder. The service watches it once a second. A kick only brings a failed host's next start forward, never sooner than five seconds after the previous start and never while a start or restart is running; the first four reasons above cannot pass by retrying, so they get one kicked start between two backoff starts. A kick to a running host never stops it: it probes the host, which restarts only when the probe fails and the host is idle.

The probe (execution_host_unhealthy) reads the host's receipt, its control socket and one execution/status answer, and on a Mac that shares native chats also the app's engine. The host answers execution/status ahead of any work it has queued, and only two failed probes in a row count; a verdict about a host that another start replaced while the probe ran is dropped:

Reason Meaning
receipt_mismatch owner.json no longer says this service runs the host at its control socket.
socket_mismatch The control link, or the SDK socket it names, is gone or replaced, for example by the periodic /tmp cleanup; no adapter can reach the host.
status_timeout execution/status did not answer within 5 s.
status_failed The socket refused the connection or answered for another process.
sdk_changed The app's engine was replaced under a host that shares native chats, as an app update does. The file is hashed once per host start and again only when its size, times or inode change.

The service also runs the watchdog heartbeat (health) in-process for the configuration its plan names; stopping the service stops it and a smoke run still in progress.

gateway health records no telemetry events of its own. Its service and errors checks read this log for the last 15 minutes, using only the fields at, event, component, kind, method, code, site, errorClass and rejection: execution_host_failed, component_exit per kind, rpc_error for a chat-session method refused with -32001 or with rejection other, gateway_features_trimmed with site retry followed by such a refusal, and native_sharing_unavailable and native_sharing_fallback.

Native relay records

The native relay writes its own JSON records to its managed log, one record per write: session lifecycle, session_activity and session_ended with transport counters, transport_activity, and audited SDK transport events (sdk_log). Client and stream IDs appear only as per-process hashes, and SDK message text is never printed. See native connected machines.
